title.zh: 卷九十五 列傳第二十 高儉五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄
title.en: Volume 95 Biographies 20: Gao Jian and Fifth Generation Descendents: Gao Zhong, Dou Weizhi, Douzhi, Dou Gui, Dou Cong, Dou Kang, Dou Jing, Dou Dan, Dou Zhi, Dou Congsun: Dou Dexuan
title.raw: 卷九十五 列傳第二十 高儉五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄 Volume 95 Biographies 20: Gao Jian and Fifth Generation Descendents: Gao Zhong, Dou Weizhi, Douzhi, Dou Gui, Dou Cong, Dou Kang, Dou Jing, Dou Dan, Dou Zhi, Dou Congsun: Dou Dexuan

sentences.zh: 高檢子:履行 審行 真行 五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄

translations.literal: Gao Jian's sons: Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing; fifth-generation descendant: Chong; Dou Wei's nephews: Gui, Cong, and Kang; grandnephews: Jing and Dan; nephew: Jin; great-grandnephew: Dexuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jian — sons Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing; fifth-generation descendant Chong; Dou Wei's nephews Gui, Cong, and Kang; grandnephews Jing and Dan; nephew Jin; great-grandnephew Dexuan.

sentences.zh: 高儉，字士廉，以字顯，齊清河王岳之孫，父勵樂安王，入隋為洮州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Jian, courtesy name Shilian, was known by his courtesy name. He was grandson of Prince Yue of Qinghe of Northern Qi; his father Li was Prince of Le'an; entering Sui, he served as Prefect of Tao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jian, whose courtesy name Shilian was the name by which he was known, was a grandson of Prince Yue of Qinghe under the Northern Qi. His father Li held the title Prince of Le'an and, after the Sui unification, became prefect of Tao.

sentences.zh: 士廉敏惠有度量，狀貌若畫，觀書一見輒誦，敏於占對。

translations.literal: Shilian was clever and magnanimous, his appearance as if painted; upon seeing a book once he could recite it, and he was quick in repartee.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian was quick-witted and broad-minded, with features so fine they seemed painted. He could recite a text after a single reading and was exceptionally sharp in conversation.

sentences.zh: 隋司隸大夫薛道衡、起居舍人崔祖浚皆宿臣顯重，與為忘年友，繇是有名。

translations.literal: The Sui officials Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Gentleman of the Household, were both veteran ministers of great standing; they became friends despite the age gap, and thereby he gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: He became friends across the generations with two eminent Sui veterans — Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Gentleman of the Household — and through them won a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 自以齊宗室，不欲廣交，屏居終南山下。

translations.literal: Considering himself a member of the Qi imperial clan, he did not wish to form wide connections and lived in seclusion at the foot of Mount Zhongnan.
translations.idiomatic: As a scion of the Qi royal house, he avoided broad social ties and withdrew to live quietly at the foot of Mount Zhongnan.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎高孝基勸之仕，仁壽中，舉文才甲科，補治禮郎。

translations.literal: Gao Xiaoji, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, urged him to enter office; in the Renshou era he was nominated in the top class of the literary talent examination and was appointed Gentleman for Managing Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiaoji, vice minister of personnel, persuaded him to take office. During the Renshou reign he passed the literary examination in the highest class and was appointed a gentleman for managing rites.

sentences.zh: 斛斯政奔高麗，坐與善，貶為硃鳶主簿，以母老不可居瘴癘地，乃留妻鮮于奉養而行。

translations.literal: When Husizheng fled to Goguryeo, Shilian was implicated for association with him and demoted to Registrar of Zhuyuan; because his mother was old and could not live in a miasmic region, he left his wife Xianyu to care for her and went alone.
translations.idiomatic: After Husizheng defected to Goguryeo, Shilian was punished for their association and demoted to registrar at Zhuyuan in Annam. His mother was too old to endure the southern climes, so he left his wife Xianyu to tend her and set out alone.

sentences.zh: 會世大亂，京師阻絕，交趾太守丘和署司法書佐。

translations.literal: As the age fell into great disorder and the capital was cut off, Qiu He, Administrator of Jiaozhi, appointed him Judicial Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed into chaos and the capital was unreachable, Qiu He, administrator of Jiaozhi, appointed him judicial secretary.

sentences.zh: 時欽州俚帥寧長真以兵侵交趾，和懼，欲出迎，士廉曰：「長真兵雖多，縣軍遠客，勢不得久，城中勝兵尚可戰，奈何受制於人？」

translations.literal: At that time Ning Changzhen, a Li chieftain of Qin Prefecture, invaded Jiaozhi with troops. Qiu He was afraid and wished to go out to submit. Shilian said: "Though Changzhen's troops are numerous, his army is far from home and cannot stay long. The city's fit soldiers can still fight — why submit to another's will?"
translations.idiomatic: When Ning Changzhen, a Li chieftain from Qin, marched on Jiaozhi, Qiu He panicked and prepared to surrender. Shilian objected: "Changzhen may have numbers, but his men are far from home and cannot sustain a siege. We still have able troops in the city — why let ourselves be dictated to?"

sentences.zh: 和因命為行軍司馬，逆擊破之。

translations.literal: Qiu He thereupon appointed him Campaigning Marshal and, counterattacking, defeated the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu He then named him campaigning marshal, and Shilian led a counterattack that routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使徇嶺南，武德五年與和來降，於是秦王領雍州牧，薦士廉為治中，親重之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu sent envoys to pacify Lingnan, in the fifth year of Wude Shilian came to submit with Qiu He. The Prince of Qin was then Governor of Yong Prefecture; he recommended Shilian as Administrator and treated him with personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu sent agents to bring Lingnan into submission, Shilian surrendered with Qiu He in Wude 5. The Prince of Qin, then governor of Yong, recommended him as administrator and held him in high personal regard.

sentences.zh: 隱太子與王隙已熾，乃與長孫無忌密計計定，是日率吏卒釋囚授甲，趨芳林門助戰。

translations.literal: When the rift between the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin had grown acute, Shilian secretly laid plans with Zhangsun Wuji; that day he led clerks and soldiers, released prisoners, armed them, and rushed to the Fanglin Gate to aid in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: As the feud between the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin reached its breaking point, Shilian and Zhangsun Wuji laid their plans in secret. On the day of the coup he led clerks and troops, freed prisoners, armed them, and hurried to Fanglin Gate to fight.

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，授右庶子。

translations.literal: When the Prince became Crown Prince, Shilian was appointed Right Vice Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince became crown prince, Shilian was made right vice tutor.

sentences.zh: 進侍中，封義興郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 坐匿王珪奏不時上，左授安州都督。

translations.literal: For concealing Wang Gui's memorial and not forwarding it in time, he was demoted to Military Governor of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to military governor of An for having withheld Wang Gui's memorial and failed to submit it promptly.

sentences.zh: 進益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Chief Administrator of the Great Area Command of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to chief administrator of the Yizhou area command.

sentences.zh: 蜀人畏鬼而惡疾，雖父母病皆委去，望舍投餌哺之，昆弟不相假財。

translations.literal: The people of Shu feared ghosts and loathed illness; even when parents were sick they abandoned them, casting food from afar into their dwellings; brothers would not lend one another money.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu feared spirits and shunned the sick. Even parents were abandoned in illness, with food tossed in from outside the house; brothers would not lend one another money.

sentences.zh: 士廉為設條教，辯告督勵，風俗翕然為變。

translations.literal: Shilian established regulations, explained and exhorted the people, and the customs swiftly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian issued regulations, explained the law, and urged compliance until local customs changed almost overnight.

sentences.zh: 又引諸生講授經藝，學校復興。

translations.literal: He also brought in students to lecture on the classics, and the schools flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: He also invited scholars to teach the classics, and the schools were revived.

sentences.zh: 秦時李冰導汶江水灌田，瀕水者頃千金，民相侵冒。

translations.literal: In Qin times Li Bing had channeled the Min River to irrigate fields; land along the water was worth a thousand gold per acre, and the people encroached on one another.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin times Li Bing had diverted the Min to irrigate the plain; waterfront plots were worth fortunes, and neighbors constantly encroached on one another's land.

sentences.zh: 士廉附故渠廝引旁出，以廣溉道，人以富饒。

translations.literal: Shilian attached to the old canal and drew side channels outward to broaden the irrigation ways, and the people grew prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian extended the old canal with branch channels to widen irrigation, and the people grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，進封許國公。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was advanced to Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital as minister of personnel, he was advanced to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 雅負裁鑒，又詳氏譜，所署州，人地無不當者。

translations.literal: He was famed for judgment in appointments and was expert in clan genealogies; in every prefecture he assigned, man and place were never ill matched.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for his eye in appointments and deeply versed in genealogies, he never mismatched a man to his post or region.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，攝司空，營山陵；

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Shilian acted as Minister of Works and oversaw the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died, Shilian served as acting minister of works and supervised construction of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 加特進，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was given the extraordinary rank of Special Advance and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He received the extraordinary rank of Special Advance and was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 士廉三世居此官，世榮其貴。

translations.literal: For three generations the family had held this office, and the age honored their eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of his family had held that office, and their eminence was the envy of the age.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸洛陽，太子監國，命攝少師。

translations.literal: When Taizong visited Luoyang and the Crown Prince supervised the state, Shilian was ordered to act as Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong went to Luoyang and the crown prince governed at the capital, Shilian was appointed acting junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 手詔曰：「端拱三川，不憂關中者，以屬卿也。」

translations.literal: An imperial autograph edict said: "That I can sit at ease in the Three Rivers region and not worry about Guanzhong is because I entrust it to you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand: "That I can remain at ease in the east and not fret over Guanzhong is because I leave it in your hands."

sentences.zh: 久之，請致仕，聽解僕射，加開府儀同三司、同中書門下三品，知政事。

translations.literal: After a long while he requested retirement; he was permitted to resign the vice directorship and was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag, Co-equal with the Three Departments, Third Rank, and charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In time he asked to retire. He was released from the vice directorship but given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag, made co-equal with the three departments at third rank, and kept in charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝伐高麗，皇太子監國駐定州，又攝太傅，同掌機務。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, the Crown Prince supervised the state from Ding Prefecture; Shilian again acted as Grand Tutor and jointly managed critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Goguryeo, the crown prince governed from Dingzhou; Shilian again served as acting grand tutor and shared control of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 太子令曰：「寡人資公訓道，而比聽政，據桉對公，情所未安，所司宜別設桉奉太傅。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince ordered: "I rely on the Duke's instruction, yet in recent audiences at court I sit at the desk facing him, which sits ill with me; the relevant offices should set up a separate desk for the Grand Tutor."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ordered: "I depend on your guidance, yet in court I sit at my desk facing you, which I find awkward. The staff should provide a separate desk for the grand tutor."

sentences.zh: 士廉固辭。

translations.literal: Shilian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 士廉進止詳華，凡有獻納，搢紳皆屬以目。

translations.literal: Shilian's deportment in court was measured and splendid; whenever he offered counsel, the gentry all turned their eyes to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian's bearing at court was dignified and polished; whenever he spoke, the officials all looked to him.

sentences.zh: 奏議未嘗不焚稿，家人無見者。

translations.literal: He always burned his memorial drafts; none in his household ever saw them.
translations.idiomatic: He always burned his draft memorials; not even his family ever saw them.

sentences.zh: 士廉少識太宗非常人，以所出女歸之，是為文德皇后。

translations.literal: In youth Shilian recognized that Taizong was no ordinary man and gave him his daughter in marriage; she became Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Shilian saw that the future Taizong was no ordinary man and gave him his daughter in marriage — the future Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 及遺令墓不得它藏，惟置衣一襲與平生所好書示先王典訓可用終始者。

translations.literal: In his testament he ordered that the tomb hold nothing else — only one suit of clothes and the books he had loved in life, those showing the ancient kings' teachings useful from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: His will directed that nothing else be buried with him — only a single suit of clothes and the books he had cherished, those ancient teachings of use from first to last.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗以山東士人尚閥閱，後雖衰，子孫猶負世望，嫁娶必多取貲，故人謂之賣昏。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizong had observed that the gentry east of the mountains prized pedigree; though later in decline, their descendants still bore the prestige of old families and demanded heavy bride-price at marriage, so people called it "selling a wedding."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had long noted that eastern gentry families prized pedigree. Though their power had waned, their descendants still traded on old prestige and demanded lavish bride-prices — what people called "selling a marriage."

sentences.zh: 由是詔士廉與韋挺、岑文本、令狐德棻責天下譜諜，參考史傳，檢正真偽，進忠賢，退悖惡，先宗室，後外戚，退新門，進舊望，右膏粱，左寒畯，合二百九十三姓，千六百五十一家，為九等，號曰《氏族志》，而崔幹仍居第一。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Shilian, together with Wei Ting, Cen Wenti, and Linghu Defen, to compile the empire's genealogies, consult historical records, verify truth and falsehood, advance the loyal and worthy and demote the perverse and wicked, put the imperial clan first and affinal kin after, demote new families and advance old prestige, favor the wellborn on the right and the humble on the left — in all two hundred ninety-three surnames and one thousand six hundred fifty-one households in nine grades, titled Records of Clans — yet Cui Gan still ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore charged Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenti, and Linghu Defen to compile the empire's genealogies, cross-check them against history, promote the worthy and demote the corrupt, rank the imperial clan before affinal kin, favor old houses over parvenus, and place the wellborn above the humble. The result listed 293 surnames in 1,651 households across nine grades, published as Records of Clans — yet Cui Gan still headed the list.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我于崔、盧、李、鄭無嫌，顧其世衰，不復冠冕，猶恃舊地以取貲，不肖子偃然自高，販鬻松檟，不解人間何為貴之？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I bear no grudge against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng clans, but their age has declined and they no longer fill high office, yet still rely on old standing to extract wealth; unworthy sons hold themselves aloft and trade in pine and cypress for profit — I do not understand why the world still esteems them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have nothing against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng families, but their day is past. They no longer produce ministers, yet still milk their old prestige for money. Their worthless sons strut as if noble and peddle funeral timber for profit — why does anyone still honor them?

sentences.zh: 齊據河北，梁、陳在江南，雖有人物，偏方下國，無可貴者，故以崔、盧、王、謝為重。

translations.literal: Qi held Hebei, Liang and Chen were in the south — though they had men of talent, they were peripheral lesser states with nothing to esteem, so the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were held in weight.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held the north, Liang and Chen the south — talented men they had, but as marginal states they counted for little. That is why the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were once so prized.

sentences.zh: 今謀士勞臣以忠孝學藝從我定天下者，何容納貨舊門，向聲背實，買昏為榮耶？

translations.literal: Now the strategists and toiling ministers who followed me in loyalty, filial piety, learning, and arts to settle the realm — how can they accept goods from old houses, heed reputation over substance, and take buying a marriage as glory?
translations.idiomatic: The counselors and warriors who followed me in loyalty, learning, and merit to win the empire — how can they pay bride-price to decayed old clans, chase empty reputation over real worth, and treat a bought marriage as an honor?

sentences.zh: 太上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言，其次有爵為公、卿、大夫，世世不絕，此謂之門戶。

translations.literal: Supreme is establishing virtue, next establishing merit, next establishing words, next enfeoffment as duke, minister, or grandee passing from generation to generation without end — this is what is called a house.
translations.idiomatic: First comes establishing virtue, then merit, then literary legacy, then hereditary rank as duke, minister, or grandee — that is what makes a true house.

sentences.zh: 今皆反是，豈不惑邪？

translations.literal: Now all is the reverse — is this not delusion?
translations.idiomatic: Today everything is reversed — is that not madness?

sentences.zh: 朕以今日冠冕為等級高下。」

translations.literal: I take today's caps and sashes as the measure of rank high and low."
translations.idiomatic: I will rank families by the offices they hold today."

sentences.zh: 遂以崔幹為第三姓，班其書天下。

translations.literal: He then placed Cui Gan as the third surname and promulgated the book throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He demoted the Cui to third rank and had the register published empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，許敬宗以不敘武后世，又李義府恥其家無名，更以孔志約、楊仁卿、史玄道、呂才等十二人刊定之，裁廣類例，合二百三十五姓，二千二百八十七家，帝自敘所以然。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong, Xu Jingzong, because Empress Wu's lineage was not recorded, and Li Yifu ashamed that his family had no name, revised it with twelve men including Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, and Lü Cai, broadening categories — in all two hundred thirty-five surnames and two thousand two hundred eighty-seven households; the Emperor himself explained the reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Xu Jingzong — who had omitted Empress Wu's line — and Li Yifu, ashamed of his obscure birth, commissioned Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, Lü Cai, and eight others to revise the register. They expanded the categories to 235 surnames in 2,287 households; the emperor himself explained the new principles.

sentences.zh: 以四後姓、酅公、介公及三公、太子三師、開府儀同三司、尚書僕射為第一姓，文武二品及知政事三品為第二姓，各以品位高下敘之，凡九等，取身及昆弟子孫，余屬不入，改為《姓氏錄》。

translations.literal: The four empresses' surnames, the Duke of Xi, the Duke of Jie, and the Three Dukes, the Crown Prince's Three Preceptors, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag, and Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs were made the first surname; civil and military officials of the second rank and third-rank participants in governance were the second surname; each was ordered by office rank high and low — nine grades in all, including only oneself and brothers, sons, and grandsons; other kin were excluded. It was retitled Record of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: First rank went to the four empresses' clans, the dukes of Xi and Jie, the three dukes, the crown prince's tutors, grandees of splendid happiness, and vice directors. Second rank covered second-rank officials and third-rank councilors, all ordered by current office. Nine grades listed only the man, his brothers, sons, and grandsons — no collateral kin. The work was retitled Record of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 當時軍功入五品者，皆升譜限，搢紳恥焉，目為「勳格」。

translations.literal: At the time all who entered the fifth rank by military merit were raised in genealogical standing; the gentry were ashamed and called it the "merit register."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who reached fifth rank through military service was elevated in the register. The gentry were mortified and dubbed it the "merit list."

sentences.zh: 義府奏悉索《氏族志》燒之。

translations.literal: Yifu memorialized to have all copies of Records of Clans seized and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu petitioned to have every copy of Records of Clans confiscated and burned.

sentences.zh: 又詔後魏隴西李寶，太原王瓊，滎陽鄭溫，范陽盧子遷、盧澤、盧輔，清河崔宗伯、崔元孫，前燕博陵崔懿，晉趙郡李楷，凡七姓十家，不得自為昏；

translations.literal: It was further decreed that the seven surnames and ten houses — Li Bao of Longxi under Later Wei, Wang Qiong of Taiyuan, Zheng Wen of Xingyang, Lu Ziqian, Lu Ze, and Lu Fu of Fanyang, Cui Zongbo and Cui Yuansun of Qinghe, Cui Yi of Boling under Former Yan, and Li Kai of Zhao under Jin — might not intermarry among themselves;
translations.idiomatic: An edict also barred intermarriage among the seven great surnames in ten houses: the Li of Longxi, Wang of Taiyuan, Zheng of Xingyang, three branches of the Lu of Fanyang, two branches of the Cui of Qinghe, the Cui of Boling, and the Li of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 三品以上納幣不得過三百匹，四品五品二百，六品七品百，悉為歸裝，夫氏禁受陪門財。

translations.literal: bride-price for third rank and above might not exceed three hundred bolts of silk, for fourth and fifth ranks two hundred, for sixth and seventh ranks one hundred — all to be the bride's dowry; the husband's clan was forbidden to accept door-accompanying wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Bride-price was capped at 300 bolts for third rank and above, 200 for fourth and fifth, 100 for sixth and seventh — all to form the bride's trousseau. The groom's family was forbidden to accept supplementary marriage payments.

sentences.zh: 先是，後魏太和中，定四海望族，以寶等為冠。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era of Later Wei, the great clans of the four seas were fixed, with Bao and the others at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Northern Wei's Taihe era, the empire's great clans had been ranked with the Li of Longxi and their peers at the top.

sentences.zh: 其後矜尚門地，故《氏族志》一切降之。

translations.literal: Thereafter they prized pedigree, so Records of Clans demoted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as pedigree pride revived, Records of Clans had demoted them all.

sentences.zh: 王妃、主婿皆取當世勳貴名臣家，未嘗尚山東舊族。

translations.literal: Imperial princesses' husbands and princesses' consorts were all taken from contemporary meritorious and eminent ministerial houses; they never favored the old clans east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law were drawn from contemporary meritocratic and ministerial families, never from the old eastern aristocracy.

sentences.zh: 後房玄齡、魏徵、李勣復與昏，故望不減，然每姓第其房望，雖一姓中，高下縣隔。

translations.literal: Later Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Li Ji again intermarried with them, so prestige did not decline; yet within each surname branches were ranked by prestige, and even within one surname high and low were vastly separated.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Li Ji married into those clans, their prestige revived. Yet within each surname branches were ranked, and even cousins could stand worlds apart in status.

sentences.zh: 李義府為子求昏不得，始奏禁焉。

translations.literal: When Li Yifu could not obtain a marriage for his son, he first memorialized for the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yifu failed to secure a marriage for his son into those houses, he petitioned for the ban.

sentences.zh: 其後天下衰宗落譜，昭穆所不齒者，皆稱「禁昏家」，益自貴，凡男女皆潛相聘娶，天子不能禁，世以為敝雲。

translations.literal: Thereafter declining clans dropped from the registers, those not admitted in the line of descent all called themselves "forbidden-marriage houses," prized themselves all the more, and men and women secretly betrothed one another; the Son of Heaven could not forbid it — the age regarded it as a abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Declining branches struck from the registers began calling themselves "forbidden-marriage houses" and grew prouder still. Couples arranged secret betrothals the throne could not stop — a custom the age regarded as a corruption.

sentences.zh: 士廉六子，履行、審行、真行有名。

translations.literal: Shilian had six sons; Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing were famed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian had six sons; Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing were the best known.

sentences.zh: 子 履行

translations.literal: Son: Lüxing
translations.idiomatic: Son — Lüxing

sentences.zh: 履行居母喪毀甚，太宗諭使強食。

translations.literal: Lüxing in mourning for his mother was so devastated that Taizong urged him to force himself to eat.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning Lüxing grieved so severely that Taizong ordered him to eat by force.

sentences.zh: 尚東陽公主，襲爵。

translations.literal: He married Princess Dongyang and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Dongyang and inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 繇戶部尚書為益州大都督府長史，政有名。

translations.literal: From Minister of Revenue he became Chief Administrator of the Great Area Command of Yizhou; his governance won renown.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as minister of revenue he became chief administrator of Yizhou, where his governance earned a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 坐長孫無忌，左授洪州都督，改永州刺史。

translations.literal: Implicated in Zhangsun Wuji's case, he was demoted to Military Governor of Hong Prefecture and then transferred to Prefect of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Caught up in Zhangsun Wuji's fall, he was demoted to military governor of Hongzhou and later made prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 真行

translations.literal: Son: Zhenxing
translations.idiomatic: Son — Zhenxing

sentences.zh: 真行至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Zhenxing rose to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxing rose to general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 其子岐連章懷太子事，詔令自誡切，真行以佩刀刺殺之，斷首棄道上，高宗鄙其為，貶睦州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Qi was implicated in the Heir Apparent Zhanghuai's affair; an edict ordered him to admonish himself sternly. Zhenxing stabbed him to death with his belt knife, severed the head, and cast it on the road. Gaozong despised the act and demoted Zhenxing to Prefect of Mu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi was implicated in Crown Prince Zhanghuai's conspiracy; the court ordered Zhenxing to discipline him harshly. Instead Zhenxing stabbed him with his dagger, cut off his head, and threw it in the street. Gaozong was disgusted and demoted him to prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 審行

translations.literal: Son: Shenxing
translations.idiomatic: Son — Shenxing

sentences.zh: 審行自戶部侍郎貶渝州刺史。

translations.literal: Shenxing was demoted from Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue to Prefect of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing was demoted from vice minister of revenue to prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五世孫 重

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant: Chong
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-generation descendant — Chong

sentences.zh: 士廉五世孫重，字文明，以明經中第，李巽表鹽鐵轉運巡官，善職，凡十年，進累司門郎中。

translations.literal: Chong, Shilian's fifth-generation descendant, courtesy name Wenming, passed the Classics examination; Li Xun recommended him as Salt and Iron Transport Circuit Inspector. He served well for ten years in all and was advanced through repeated promotions to Director of the Department of Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, Shilian's fifth-generation descendant, courtesy name Wenming, passed the classics examination. Li Xun recommended him as salt-and-iron transport inspector; he served capably for ten years and rose to director of the department of passes.

sentences.zh: 敬宗慎置侍講學士，重以簡厚惇正，與崔郾偕選，再擢國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Jingzong carefully appointed Lecturing Scholars; Chong, for his simplicity, generosity, and integrity, was chosen together with Cui Yan and was twice promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong carefully chose lecturing scholars; Chong, noted for his plain integrity, was selected with Cui Yan and twice promoted to chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 文宗好《左氏春秋》，命分列國各為書，成四十篇。

translations.literal: Wenzong loved the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and ordered that each state be made a separate book — forty chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong loved the Zuo Commentary and ordered each state to be treated as a separate volume — forty chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 與鄭覃刊定《九經》于石。

translations.literal: Together with Zheng Tan he collated the Nine Classics on stone.
translations.idiomatic: With Zheng Tan he carved the corrected Nine Classics in stone.

sentences.zh: 出為鄂嶽觀察使，以美政被褒。

translations.literal: He went out as Observation Commissioner of E and Yue and was praised for excellent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as observation commissioner of E and Yue, he was commended for excellent governance.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Guest of the Crown Prince with detached service at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made guest of the crown prince with detached duty at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：古者受姓受氏以旌有功，是時人皆土著，故名宗望姓，舉郡國自表，而譜系興焉，所以推敘昭穆，使百代不得相亂也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In antiquity one received surname and clan-name to honor merit. At that time all people were settled natives, so clans were named by ancestral seat and surname; each commandery and kingdom presented its own register, and genealogies arose — thereby to arrange senior and junior lines so that a hundred generations would not fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: In antiquity surnames and clan names honored merit. People were rooted to their native places, so clans took their names from ancestral seats and presented registers by commandery and kingdom. Genealogies arose to order senior and junior lines across the generations.

sentences.zh: 遭晉播遷，胡醜亂華，百宗蕩析，士去墳墓，子孫猶挾系錄，以示所承，而閥閥顯者，至賣昏求財，汨喪廉恥。

translations.literal: When Jin was driven into exile and barbarian hosts ravaged China, a hundred clans were scattered; gentlemen left their ancestral graves, yet descendants still carried genealogical records to show their descent. Those of eminent pedigree came to sell marriages for profit and drowned integrity.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin exodus and barbarian invasions shattered the clans, scholars fled their ancestral graves, yet descendants still clung to genealogies to prove their lineage. Great houses sold marriages for profit and abandoned all shame.

sentences.zh: 唐初流弊仍甚，天子屢抑不為衰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang the abuses remained severe; the Son of Heaven repeatedly suppressed them, yet they did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang saw the same abuses; emperors repeatedly tried to curb them, yet they persisted.

sentences.zh: 至中葉，風教又薄，譜錄都廢，公靡常產之拘，士亡舊德之傳，言李悉出隴西，言劉悉出彭城，悠悠世詐，訖無考按，冠冕皁隸，混為一區，可太息哉！

translations.literal: By the mid-dynasty customs had thinned again; genealogies were wholly abandoned. Dukes were no longer bound by fixed estates, scholars lost the transmission of old virtue — every Li was said to come from Longxi, every Liu from Pengcheng. Through long ages fraud ran on with no verification; caps and sashes and black-clad servants were mixed in one mass — alas!
translations.idiomatic: By mid-Tang morals had thinned again and genealogies were abandoned. Great families lost their fixed estates; scholars lost their ancestral traditions. Every Li claimed Longxi, every Liu Pengcheng. Fraud ran unchecked for generations until nobles and commoners were indistinguishable — a cause for deep lament.

sentences.zh: 竇威，字文蔚，岐州平陸人。

translations.literal: Dou Wei, courtesy name Wenwei, was a native of Pinglu in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei, courtesy name Wenwei, was from Pinglu in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父熾，在周為上柱國，入隋為太傅，太穆皇后，其從兄弟女也。

translations.literal: His father Chi was Upper Pillar of State under Zhou; entering Sui he became Grand Tutor. Empress Taimu was the daughter of his father's cousin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi was a Zhou upper pillar of state and became Sui grand tutor. Empress Taimu was his father's cousin's daughter.

sentences.zh: 威沈邃有器局，貫覽群言，家世貴，子弟皆喜武力，獨威尚文，諸兄詆為書癡。

translations.literal: Wei was deep and far-sighted with great capacity, thoroughly versed in all writings. The family had long been noble; the younger men all loved martial arts, but Wei alone honored letters, and his brothers mocked him as a book fool.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was deep-minded and magnanimous, widely read in the classics. His family was aristocratic and his brothers favored martial pursuits, but Wei devoted himself to learning — they called him a bookworm.

sentences.zh: 內史令李德林舉秀異，授秘書郎，當遷不肯調者十年，故其學益博。

translations.literal: Li Delin, Director of the Palace Secretariat, recommended him as outstanding talent; he was appointed Secretary. When due for transfer he refused reassignment for ten years, and thereby his learning grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin, director of the palace secretariat, recommended him as outstanding talent and appointed him secretary. He refused promotion for ten years to keep studying, and his learning grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 而諸兄以軍功位通顯矣，薄威職閑冗，更謂曰：「昔仲尼積學成聖，猶棲遲不偶，汝尚何求耶？」

translations.literal: His brothers had already reached high office through military merit and looked down on Wei's post as idle and trivial, saying further: "In old times Confucius amassed learning and became a sage, yet still lingered without success — what more do you seek?"
translations.idiomatic: His brothers had risen through military merit and scorned his quiet post. They told him: "Even Confucius, for all his learning, struggled without success — what are you still chasing?"

sentences.zh: 威笑不答。

translations.literal: Wei smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wei only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀辟為記室，威以秀多不法，謝疾去。

translations.literal: Prince Xiu of Shu recruited him as Recorder; Wei, finding the prince often lawless, pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Shu appointed him recorder, but Wei, finding the prince lawless, pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 秀廢，府屬皆得罪，威獨免。

translations.literal: When Xiu was deposed, all staff were punished; Wei alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was deposed, every member of his staff was punished — Wei alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累遷內史舍人，數諫忤旨，轉考功郎中，後坐事免。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Palace Secretariat; he remonstrated often against the Emperor's will, was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Evaluations, and later was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daye he rose to palace secretariat attendant but offended the emperor with repeated remonstrances and was transferred to director of evaluations, then dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後寢疾，帝臨問，及卒，哭之慟。

translations.literal: Later he took to his bed; the Emperor visited him in inquiry, and when he died wept for him in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill the emperor visited his bedside; at his death the emperor wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 贈同州刺史，追封延安郡公，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Prefect of Tong Prefecture, ennobled posthumously as Duke of Yan'an Commandery, with posthumous title Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made prefect of Tong, ennobled as Duke of Yan'an, with the posthumous name Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 威性儉素，家不樹產，比喪，無餘貲，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: Wei was frugal and plain by nature; the family accumulated no property. At his death there was no surplus wealth; his testament ordered a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei lived simply and left no family wealth. At his death there was nothing left; his will called for a plain burial.

sentences.zh: 詔皇太子、百官臨送。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Crown Prince and all officials to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the entire court were ordered to attend his funeral.

sentences.zh: 侄 軌

translations.literal: Nephew: Gui
translations.idiomatic: Nephew — Gui

sentences.zh: 兄子軌，字士則。

translations.literal: His brother's son Gui, courtesy name Shize.
translations.idiomatic: His brother's son Gui, courtesy name Shize.

sentences.zh: 父恭，仕周為雍州牧、酂國公。

translations.literal: His father Gong served Zhou as Governor of Yong Prefecture and Duke of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong served Zhou as governor of Yong and duke of Zan.

sentences.zh: 軌性剛果有威，大業中，為資陽郡東曹掾，去官歸。

translations.literal: Gui was firm, resolute, and commanding; in the Daye era he was Eastern Bureau Clerk of Ziyang Commandery, then left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was bold and formidable. Under Daye he served as eastern bureau clerk of Ziyang, then resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 高祖起兵，軌募眾千餘人迎謁長春宮。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised his army, Gui recruited more than a thousand men and went to pay homage at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rebelled, Gui raised over a thousand men and went to Changchun Palace to join him.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜良馬十匹，使略地渭南，下永豐倉，收兵五千，從平京師。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed ten fine horses, and sent him to seize territory south of the Wei, take Yongfeng Granary, gather five thousand troops, and follow in pacifying the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to seize the Wei south bank, capture Yongfeng Granary, raise five thousand troops, and help take the capital.

sentences.zh: 封贊皇縣公，為大丞相諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang County and made Consulting Staff Officer to the Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as duke of Zanhuang and made consulting officer to the grand chancellor.

sentences.zh: 稽胡賊五萬掠宜春，詔軌討之。

translations.literal: Ji-hu bandits fifty thousand plundered Yichun; an edict ordered Gui to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand Ji-hu bandits raided Yichun; the court ordered Gui to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 次黃欽山，遇賊乘高叢射，眾為卻。

translations.literal: Halting at Huangqin Mountain, they met bandits shooting from high thickets, and the troops were driven back.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangqin Mountain they ran into bandits firing from the heights through dense brush, and the army fell back.

sentences.zh: 軌斬部將十四人，更拔其次代之，身擁數百騎殿，令曰：「聞鼓不進者斬。」

translations.literal: Gui beheaded fourteen subordinate commanders, replaced them with their next in rank, personally led several hundred horsemen in the rearguard, and ordered: "Whoever hears the drum and does not advance will be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Gui executed fourteen commanders, promoted their seconds to replace them, took personal command of several hundred horsemen in the rear, and proclaimed: "Any man who hears the drum and does not advance will be executed.

sentences.zh: 既鼓，士爭赴賊，賊射不勝，大破之，斬首千級，獲男女二萬。

translations.literal: When the drum sounded, the soldiers raced at the bandits; the bandits' arrows could not prevail, and they were routed decisively — a thousand heads taken, twenty thousand men and women captured.
translations.idiomatic: At the drumbeat the men rushed the enemy; their volleys could not stop the charge. Gui crushed them, took a thousand heads, and captured twenty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 擢太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Master of Ceremonies for the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of ceremonies for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 赤排羌與薛舉叛將鐘俱仇寇漢中，拜秦州總管，討賊連戰有功，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: The Chipai Qiang and Zhong Juqiu, a defector of Xue Ju, raided Hanzhong; Gui was appointed Military Governor of Qin Prefecture, fought the bandits in successive battles with merit, and the remaining factions all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chipai Qiang and Xue Ju's turncoat general Zhong Juqiu raided Hanzhong, Gui was made military governor of Qin. He fought a series of victorious engagements and the remnants all submitted.

sentences.zh: 復酂國舊封，遷益州道行台左僕射。

translations.literal: His old enfeoffment as Duke of Zan was restored, and he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: His old ducal title of Zan was restored, and he was made left vice director of the Yizhou circuit executive.

sentences.zh: 党項引吐谷渾寇松州，詔軌與扶州刺史蔣善合援之。

translations.literal: The Tangut led Tuyuhun to raid Song Prefecture; an edict ordered Gui and Jiang Shanhe, Prefect of Fuzhou, to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut allies brought Tuyuhun raiders against Songzhou; the court ordered Gui and Fuzhou prefect Jiang Shanhe to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 善合先期至，敗之鉗川。

translations.literal: Shanhe arrived ahead of time and defeated them at Qianchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhe got there first and routed them at Qianchuan.

sentences.zh: 軌進軍臨洮，擊左封，走其眾。

translations.literal: Gui advanced to Lintao, struck Zuofeng, and drove off their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Gui marched on Lintao, attacked Zuofeng, and put the enemy to flight.

sentences.zh: 度羌必為患，始屯田松州。

translations.literal: Judging that the Qiang would surely become a menace, he began garrison farming at Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced the Qiang would remain a threat, he started frontier farming around Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔率所部兵從秦王討王世充。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to lead his troops following the Prince of Qin to campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead his troops with the Prince of Qin against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 明年，還蜀。

translations.literal: The next year he returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 軌既貴，益嚴酷，然能自勤苦，每出師臨敵，身未嘗解甲，其下有不用命即誅，至小過亦鞭棰流血，人見者皆重足股忄栗，由是蜀盜悉平。

translations.literal: Once Gui had grown eminent, he became still more harsh, yet he could torment himself with diligence; whenever he took the field against the enemy he never doffed his armor; subordinates who disobeyed were immediately executed, and even for minor faults he flogged until blood flowed — all who saw him treaded lightly and trembled on their feet, and thereby the bandits of Shu were wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated, Gui grew even more brutal, yet he drove himself as hard as any man under him: on campaign he never took off his armor; disobedience meant death, and minor infractions brought flogging until the blood ran. Everyone who encountered him walked on tiptoe, trembling on their feet — and by that means banditry in Shu was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 初，以其甥為腹心，嘗夜出，呼不時至，斬之。

translations.literal: At first he used his nephew as his trusted confidant; once at night he went out and when the nephew did not come promptly when called, he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he relied on a nephew as his right hand. One night he went out and summoned him; when the man failed to arrive promptly, Gui had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又戒家奴毋出外，忽遣奴取漿公廚，既而悔焉，曰：「要當借汝頭以明法。」

translations.literal: He also forbade his household slaves to go outside; suddenly he sent a slave to fetch gruel from the public kitchen, then regretted it and said: "I must borrow your head to clarify the law.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade his household slaves to leave the compound. Once he impulsively sent a slave to fetch gruel from the public kitchen, then regretted it and said, "I shall have to take your head to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 命斬奴，奴稱冤，監刑者疑不時決，軌並斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered the slave beheaded; the slave cried injustice, and the supervising executioner hesitated to act promptly — Gui beheaded them both.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the slave executed. The slave protested his innocence, and the overseer hesitated — so Gui had them both killed.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，賜坐禦樓，容不肅，又坐對詔，帝怒曰：「公入蜀，車騎、驃騎從者二十人，公斬誅略盡，我隴種車騎，尚不足給公。」

translations.literal: Later he entered court; granted a seat in the imperial tower, his bearing was not respectful; again seated facing the edict, the Emperor angrily said: "When you entered Shu, the twenty mounted attendants of my carriage and fast-steed escorts — you executed nearly all of them; my Longzhong cavalry escort still would not suffice for you.
translations.idiomatic: Later, summoned to court, he was granted a seat in the imperial tower but sat without proper decorum; when again seated to receive an imperial message, the emperor in anger said, "When you went to Shu you all but wiped out the twenty mounted guards I gave you — my own Longzhong cavalry escort would scarcely be enough for you.

sentences.zh: 因系詔獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was imprisoned in the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon thrown into the edict prison.

sentences.zh: 俄釋之，還鎮益州。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and returned to garrison Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was freed and sent back to command Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 軌與行台尚書韋雲起、郭行方素不協，及隱太子誅，詔至，軌內詔懷中，雲起問詔安在，軌不肯示，因執殺之。

translations.literal: Gui and the Executive Directors of State Affairs Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang had long been at odds; when the Hidden Crown Prince was executed, the edict arrived; Gui tucked the edict inside his robe; Yunqi asked where the edict was, and Gui refused to show it, then seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long been estranged from executive directors Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang. When news came of the Hidden Crown Prince's death, the edict reached Gui — he hid it in his robe. Yunqi asked to see it; Gui refused and had him seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 行方懼，奔京師，得免。

translations.literal: Xingfang was afraid, fled to the capital, and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfang fled to the capital in terror and escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 是歲，行台廢，授益州都督，加食邑戶六百。

translations.literal: That year the executive was abolished; he was appointed Military Governor of Yizhou and given six hundred additional fief households.
translations.idiomatic: That year the circuit executive was dissolved; he was made military governor of Yizhou with six hundred added fief households.

sentences.zh: 侄 琮

translations.literal: Nephew: Cong
translations.idiomatic: Nephew — Cong

sentences.zh: 軌弟琮，有武幹。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Cong had martial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Cong was a capable soldier.

sentences.zh: 大業末，犯法亡命太原，依高祖。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, having violated the law he fled as an outlaw to Taiyuan and attached himself to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Daye he fled to Taiyuan as an outlaw and placed himself under Gaozu's protection.

sentences.zh: 與秦王有憾，不自安。

translations.literal: He had a grievance with the Prince of Qin and was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed a grudge against the Prince of Qin and felt uneasy.

sentences.zh: 王方收天下豪英，降禮接之，與出入臥內，琮意乃釋。

translations.literal: The Prince was then gathering heroes from across the realm, receiving them with lowered courtesy; he admitted Cong to enter and leave his inner quarters, and Cong's resentment was thus released.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was recruiting talent from across the realm and treating men with deference; he admitted Cong to his private quarters, and Cong's suspicions eased.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，引為統軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's headquarters was established, Cong was recruited as Commanding General.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand general's headquarters was set up, Cong was made a commanding general.

sentences.zh: 從平西河，破霍邑。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Xihe and broke Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Xihe and stormed Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 授金紫光祿大夫，封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag and enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He received the rank of grand master of splendid happiness with the golden bag and was enfeoffed as duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 從劉文靜擊屈突通於潼關，敗其將桑顯和，通遁去，琮以輕騎追獲于稠桑。

translations.literal: Following Liu Wenjing he attacked Qu Tutong at Tong Pass, defeated his general Sang Xianhe; Tutong fled, and Cong with light cavalry pursued and captured him at Chousang.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Wenjing he attacked Qu Tutong at Tong Pass, routed Sang Xianhe, and when Tutong fled Cong ran him down with light cavalry and captured him at Chousang.

sentences.zh: 進兵下陝縣，拔太原倉。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Shaan County and captured Taiyuan Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Shaan County and seize Taiyuan Granary.

sentences.zh: 遷左領軍大將軍，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guards and given five hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the left guards and awarded five hundred rolls of silk and goods.

sentences.zh: 隋河陽都尉獨孤武潛謀歸款，命琮總萬騎，自柏崖迎之，逗留不進，武見殺，坐除名。

translations.literal: Dugu Wu, Sui Commander of Heyang, secretly planned to defect; Cong was ordered to command ten thousand horsemen and receive him from Baiya, but delayed and did not advance; Wu was killed, and Cong was demoted and struck from the rolls for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Heyang commander Dugu Wu plotted to defect, Cong was sent with ten thousand cavalry to meet him at Baiya — but he lingered, Wu was killed, and Cong was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 武德初，為右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Wude he served as Grand General of the Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he became grand general of the right palace guard.

sentences.zh: 時將圖洛陽，詔琮留守陝，護饟道。

translations.literal: When plans were being made to take Luoyang, an edict ordered Cong to remain and garrison Shaan, protecting the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: As the court planned the Luoyang campaign, Cong was ordered to hold Shaan and guard the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 王世充將羅士信數以兵鈔絕，琮使人說降之。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's general Luo Shixin repeatedly cut the route with raiding troops; Cong sent men to persuade him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's general Luo Shixin repeatedly raided the supply route; Cong sent envoys to win him over.

sentences.zh: 東都平，檢校晉州總管。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was made acting Military Governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern capital fell, he was made acting military governor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 從隱太子平劉黑闥，以功封譙國公，賜黃金五十斤。

translations.literal: Following the Hidden Crown Prince he pacified Liu Heita; for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Qiao and given fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Serving with the Hidden Crown Prince against Liu Heita, he earned enfeoffment as duke of Qiao and fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左衛大將軍，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Grand General of the Left Palace Guard; posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand general of the left guard, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，加贈特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was additionally given the rank of Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 5 he received the additional posthumous rank of Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 侄 抗

translations.literal: Nephew: Kang
translations.idiomatic: Nephew — Kang

sentences.zh: 威從兄子抗，字道生。

translations.literal: Wei's older brother's son Kang, courtesy name Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's elder brother's son Kang, courtesy name Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 父榮定，為隋洺州總管、陳國公，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: His father Rongding served Sui as Military Governor of Ming Prefecture and Duke of Chen; posthumous title Majestic.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rongding served the Sui as military governor of Ming and duke of Chen, posthumously titled Majestic.

sentences.zh: 母，隋文帝姊安成公主也。

translations.literal: His mother was the Elder Sister of Emperor Wen of Sui, Princess Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Emperor Wen of Sui's elder sister, Princess Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 抗美容儀，性通率，涉見圖史。

translations.literal: Kang had handsome bearing; his nature was frank and straightforward; he had browsed illustrated histories.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was handsome and open in temperament, well read in history and the classics.

sentences.zh: 以帝甥蚤貴，入太學，釋褐千牛備身、儀同三司。

translations.literal: As the Emperor's nephew he was early eminent; he entered the Imperial Academy and upon first appointment was made Palace Guard Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's nephew he rose early: he studied at the Imperial Academy and upon entering office became a palace guard attendant with the rank of grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 侍父疾，束帶五旬不弛；

translations.literal: Attending his father's illness, he kept his belt tied for fifty days without loosening it;
translations.idiomatic: While nursing his father he wore his official belt day and night for fifty days without loosening it;

sentences.zh: 居喪，哀臒過常。

translations.literal: In mourning, his grief and emaciation exceeded the norm.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning his grief left him wasted beyond ordinary measure.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，累轉梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and successively served as Prefect of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and rose through postings to prefect of Liang.

sentences.zh: 將之官，文帝幸其第，酣宴如家人禮。

translations.literal: About to take up his post, Emperor Wen visited his residence and feasted freely with the rites of family.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to take up his post, Emperor Wen visited his home and feasted with him as one of the family.

sentences.zh: 母卒，數號絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he repeatedly cried himself into unconsciousness.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death he repeatedly fainted from wailing.

sentences.zh: 詔宮人節哭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the palace women to moderate his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered palace attendants to restrain his mourning.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為岐州刺史，轉幽州總管，所至以寬惠聞。

translations.literal: After a year and more he became Prefect of Qi Prefecture, then transferred to Military Governor of You Prefecture; wherever he went he was known for leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became prefect of Qi, then military governor of You — everywhere he served he was known for clemency.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，煬帝疑抗為應，遣李子雄馳往代之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Han, Liang, rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang would respond and dispatched Li Zixiong posthaste to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang might join him and sent Li Zixiong at full speed to relieve him of command.

sentences.zh: 子雄因誣抗得諒書不奏，按鞫無狀，然坐是遂廢。

translations.literal: Zixiong therefore falsely accused Kang of having received a letter from Liang and not reporting it; investigation found no basis, yet because of this Kang was finally dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong falsely claimed Kang had received a letter from Liang and concealed it. The inquiry found nothing — but Kang was dismissed nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 抗與高祖少相狎，及楊玄感反，抗謂高祖曰：「玄感為我先耳，李氏名在圖錄，天所啟也。」

translations.literal: Kang and Gaozu had been intimate since youth; when Yang Xuangan rebelled, Kang said to Gaozu: "Xuangan acts as my forerunner; the surname Li is recorded in the prophecy rolls — Heaven has opened the way.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Gaozu had been close since youth. When Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion, Kang told Gaozu, "Xuangan goes before us — the Li are named in the prophecy rolls; Heaven itself has opened the way.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「為禍始不祥，公無妄言。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "To begin calamity is inauspicious — do not speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied, "To start the trouble would be ill-omened — speak no more of this."

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣抗出靈武，逴護長城，聞高祖已定京師，喜曰：「此吾家婿，豁達有大度，真撥亂主也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent Kang out to Lingwu to patrol and guard the Great Wall; hearing that Gaozu had secured the capital, he rejoiced and said: "This son-in-law of our house is openhanded and magnanimous — a true lord to quell disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Kang to Lingwu to patrol the Great Wall. Learning Gaozu had taken the capital, Kang exclaimed with delight, "My kinsman by marriage is broad-minded and magnanimous — a true prince to restore order."

sentences.zh: 因歸長安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之喜，握手曰：「李氏果王，何如？」

translations.literal: Gaozu seeing him was pleased, took his hand and said: "The Li have indeed become kings — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu greeted him with joy, clasped his hand, and said, "So the Li have taken the throne — what do you say to that?

sentences.zh: 因置酒為樂，授將作大匠兼納言，尋罷為左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon they set out wine for revelry; he was appointed Director of Imperial Construction concurrently Grand Counselor; soon dismissed to Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: They drank in celebration. Kang was made director of imperial construction and grand counselor, then shortly transferred to grand general of the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 帝聽朝，或引升禦坐，既退，入臥內，從容談笑，極平生歡，以兄呼之，宮中稱為舅，或留宿禁省，侍燕豫，然未嘗幹朝廷事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor held court, he sometimes drew Kang up to the imperial seat; after retiring he entered the private quarters, talked and laughed at ease, enjoying to the full their lifelong friendship — calling him elder brother; within the palace he was called Uncle; sometimes he stayed overnight in the forbidden offices, attending feasts and pleasures, yet he never meddled in court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor sometimes had Kang join him on the throne; after sessions he would take him into the private quarters for easy talk, calling him "brother" while the palace knew him as "uncle." Kang sometimes slept in the imperial offices and shared the emperor's leisure — yet never interfered in governance.

sentences.zh: 後從秦王平薛舉，功第一；

translations.literal: Later he followed the Prince of Qin in pacifying Xue Ju, his merit ranked first;
translations.idiomatic: Later he campaigned with the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju and ranked first in merit;

sentences.zh: 又從征王世充。

translations.literal: Again he followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: and again fought Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 東都平，冊勳於廟者九人，抗與從弟軌與焉。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, nine men had their achievements recorded in the ancestral temple — Kang and his younger cousin Gui were among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern capital fell, nine men were honored in the ancestral temple — Kang and his cousin Gui among them.

sentences.zh: 賜女樂一部，珍幣不貲。

translations.literal: He was given a troupe of female musicians and treasures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He received a company of court musicians and treasures beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，諡曰密。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Minister of Education; posthumous title Vigilant.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of education, posthumously titled Vigilant.

sentences.zh: 子衍、靜、誕，衍襲爵。

translations.literal: His sons Yan, Jing, and Dan — Yan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yan, Jing, and Dan; Yan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 侄孫 靜

translations.literal: Grandnephew: Jing
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew — Jing

sentences.zh: 靜字元休，在隋佐親衛，以父得罪煬帝，久不之進。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Yuanxiu, under Sui served in the personal guard; because his father had offended Emperor Yang, he long went without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, courtesy name Yuanxiu, served in the Sui imperial guard, but because his father had fallen from Emperor Yang's favor he languished without advancement.

sentences.zh: 高祖入京師，擢并州大總管府長史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the capital, Jing was promoted to Chief Administrator of the Bingzhou Grand Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital, Jing was made chief administrator of the Bingzhou grand area command.

sentences.zh: 時突厥數為邊患，糧道不屬，靜表請屯田太原，以省饋運。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly made border troubles, and supply routes were not continuous; Jing memorialized requesting garrison farming at Taiyuan to economize on transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Turk raids disrupted the frontier and supply lines; Jing proposed farming colonies around Taiyuan to cut transport costs.

sentences.zh: 議者以流亡未復，不宜重困，於是召入與裴寂、蕭瑀、封倫廷議，寂等不能屈，帝從之，歲收粟十萬斛。

translations.literal: Discussants held that refugees had not yet returned and it was unsuitable to burden them further; he was therefore summoned for court deliberation with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Lun — Ji and the others could not overcome his argument, and the Emperor followed it; the year yielded a hundred thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued refugees were not yet resettled and the plan would overburden them. Jing was called to debate Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Lun at court; none could refute him, and the emperor approved. That year the farms yielded a hundred thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 詔檢校并州大總管。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting Grand Area Commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting grand area commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又請斷石嶺以為鄣塞，制突厥之入。

translations.literal: He again requested blocking Shiling Pass as a barrier fort to restrain Turk incursions.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed fortifying Shiling Pass to block Turk raids.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，授司農卿，封信都縣男。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was appointed Minister of Revenue for Agriculture and enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu County.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded, Jing became minister of revenue for agriculture and baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 趙元楷為少卿，靜鄙其聚斂，因會官屬大言曰：「如煬帝奢侈，竭四海自奉，司農須公矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuankai served as Vice Minister; Jing despised his revenue gathering; at a gathering of subordinates he declared loudly: "Under an emperor as extravagant as Yang, draining the four seas to serve himself, the Ministry of Revenue would need a man like you.
translations.idiomatic: His vice minister Zhao Yuankai was notorious for squeezing revenue. At a staff meeting Jing declared, "Under an emperor as extravagant as Yang, draining the realm to feed his appetites, the ministry would need a man like you.

sentences.zh: 今天子躬節儉，屈一人安兆庶，惡用公哉？」

translations.literal: But today's Son of Heaven personally practices frugality, bending himself to settle the myriad people — why would he need you?
translations.idiomatic: But our emperor lives frugally and burdens himself so the people may rest — what use has he for you?

sentences.zh: 元楷大慚。

translations.literal: Yuankai was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai burned with shame.

sentences.zh: 改夏州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Xia.

sentences.zh: 突厥攜貳，諸將出征者過靜，靜為陳虜中虛實，諸將由是大克獲。

translations.literal: When the Turks became divided and rebellious, generals on campaign passed by Jing; Jing briefed them on conditions inside the barbarians, and the generals thereby achieved great captures.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turks turned restless, campaigning generals stopped to consult Jing on enemy conditions — and won great victories accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又間其部落，郁射所部鬱孤尼等九俟斤皆內附。

translations.literal: He also sowed discord among their tribes; the nine yishi chiefs including Yugu'ni under Yuju's division all submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: He also split their tribes: nine tribal chiefs under Yujue, including Yugu'ni, submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜馬百匹、羊千口。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended this and gave a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his work and awarded him a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 及禽頡利，詔處其眾河南。

translations.literal: When Jiali was captured, an edict settled his people south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiali Khan was captured, the court ordered his people settled south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 靜上書曰：「夷狄窮則搏噬，飽則群聚，不可以刑法繩、仁義教也。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized: "Barbarians when desperate bite and devour, when sated gather in herds — they cannot be bound by penal law or instructed by benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wrote: "Barbarians fight when desperate and flock together when fed — neither law nor moral teaching can truly bind them.

sentences.zh: 衣食仰給，不恃耕桑。

translations.literal: Their clothing and food depend on others' supply; they do not rely on farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: They live on what others provide and know nothing of farming or sericulture.

sentences.zh: 今損有為之民，資無知之虜，得之無益於治，失之不害於化。

translations.literal: Now to harm productive people in order to support ignorant barbarians — gaining them brings no benefit to governance, losing them harms not civilization.
translations.idiomatic: To burden productive citizens to feed ignorant nomads gains us nothing in governance and loses us nothing in civilization if reversed.

sentences.zh: 況首丘未忘，則一旦變生，犯我王略矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, if they have not forgotten their native hills, then suddenly change will arise and they will violate our royal dominion.
translations.idiomatic: And if they still yearn for their homelands, rebellion may come at any hour and violate the realm.

sentences.zh: 不如因其破亡，假以賢王一號，妻之宗女，披其土地部落，使權弱勢分，易為羈制，則世為籓臣矣。」

translations.literal: Better to take advantage of their defeat and ruin: grant them the title of a worthy prince, marry them to an imperial clanswoman, divide their lands and tribes so authority is weak and power scattered, easy to keep on rein — then they will be vassal ministers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Better to exploit their defeat: give them a nominal princely title, marry them to an imperial clanswoman, break up their lands and tribes so their power scatters — then they can be bridled for generations as vassals.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不從，然嘉其忠，優詔答曰：「北方之務，悉以相委，以卿為甯朔大使，朕無北顧憂矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor though he did not follow this, yet commended his loyalty and replied with a gracious edict: "Northern affairs I wholly entrust to you; with you as Pacification Commissioner for the North, I need not look back in worry toward the north."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not adopt the plan but praised Jing's loyalty and replied graciously: "I entrust all northern affairs to you. As Pacification Commissioner for the North, you leave me with no worry for that frontier."

sentences.zh: 再遷民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子逵，尚遂安公主，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Kui married Princess Sui'an and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui married Princess Sui'an and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 侄孫 誕

translations.literal: Grandnephew: Dan
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew — Dan

sentences.zh: 誕，隋末起家朝請郎。

translations.literal: Dan, at the end of Sui entered office as Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Dan entered service at the end of the Sui as a gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 義甯初，辟丞相府祭酒，封安豐郡公，尚襄陽公主。

translations.literal: At the start of Yining he was recruited as Libationer of the Chancellor's Office, enfeoffed Duke of Anfeng Commandery, and married to Princess Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yining he became libationer of the chancellor's office, was enfeoffed duke of Anfeng, and married Princess Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 從秦王征薛舉，為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin he campaigned against Xue Ju, serving as Secretary of the Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning with the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju, he served as marshal's secretary.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸子幼，未出宮者十余王，國司家事，皆誕主之。

translations.literal: Gaozu's sons were young; more than ten princes who had not yet left the palace — state and household affairs of their principalities were all managed by Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's sons were still young, and for more than ten princes who had not yet left the palace, Dan oversaw both the state and household affairs of their principalities.

sentences.zh: 出為梁州都督。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Military Governor of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召授右領軍大將軍，進莘國公，為宗正卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhenguan he was recalled and appointed General of the Right Wing Army, advanced to Duke of Shen, and made Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was recalled, made general of the right wing army, advanced to duke of Shen, and appointed director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 太宗與語，昏謬失對。

translations.literal: When Taizong spoke with him, he gave muddled and confused answers.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong conversed with him, Dan answered in a muddled and incoherent manner.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「誕比衰耗，不能事，朕知而任之，是謂不明。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "Dan has lately declined and can no longer serve; knowing this yet I still appointed him — that is to say, I lacked discernment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict: "Dan has lately grown feeble and can no longer serve. Knowing this, I still kept him in office — that was a failure of discernment on my part.

sentences.zh: 且為官擇人者治，為人擇官者亂。

translations.literal: Moreover, choosing men for offices brings order; choosing offices for men brings chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing the right people for office brings order; choosing offices for people brings chaos.

sentences.zh: 其以光祿大夫罷就第。」

translations.literal: Let him be dismissed as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and return to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He is to be dismissed with the rank of grand master of splendid happiness and retire to his home.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書、荊州刺史，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Public Works and Military Governor of Jing Prefecture, with the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of public works and governor of Jing, posthumously titled An.

sentences.zh: 侄 璡

translations.literal: Nephew: Jin
translations.idiomatic: Nephew — Jin

sentences.zh: 抗弟璡，字之推，性沈厚。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Zhitui, was of a deep and steady nature.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Kang's younger brother, courtesy name Zhitui, was deep and steady of temperament.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為扶風太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye under Sui he served as Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui Daye era he was administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 唐兵起，以郡歸，曆民部尚書。

translations.literal: When Tang forces rose, he submitted the commandery and successively served as Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang army rose, he surrendered his commandery and served successively as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 從秦王平薛仁杲，賜錦袍。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin he pacified Xue Rengao and was granted a brocade robe.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning with the Prince of Qin, he helped pacify Xue Rengao and was rewarded with a brocade robe.

sentences.zh: 尋鎮益州，時蜀盜賊多，皆討平之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he garrisoned Yizhou; at that time bandits in Shu were numerous, and he suppressed and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted to Yizhou, where rampant banditry in Shu was thoroughly suppressed.

sentences.zh: 與皇甫無逸不協，數相訴毀，因請入朝，至半道，詔還之。

translations.literal: He was at odds with Huangfu Wuyi; they repeatedly slandered one another; he therefore requested to enter court; halfway there, an edict ordered him to return.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Huangfu Wuyi and the two traded repeated accusations. Jin requested leave to attend court, but halfway there an edict sent him back.

sentences.zh: 璡內憂恐。

translations.literal: Jin was inwardly anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was inwardly gripped with anxiety and fear.

sentences.zh: 會使者至，璡引宴臥內，厚餉遺。

translations.literal: It happened that an envoy arrived; Jin brought him in to banquet in his private quarters and gave him lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy arrived, Jin entertained him in his bedchamber and lavished gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 無逸以聞，坐免官。

translations.literal: Wuyi reported this, and Jin was removed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi reported the matter, and Jin was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授秘書監，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made director of the secretariat and enfeoffed duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遷將作大匠，詔脩洛陽宮，鑿池起山，務極侈浮，費不勝算。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhenguan he was transferred to Chief Artisan for Palace Construction; ordered to repair Luoyang Palace, he dug ponds and raised artificial hills, striving for utmost extravagance; costs were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he became chief artisan for palace construction. Ordered to renovate Luoyang Palace, he dug ponds, piled up artificial hills, and pursued extravagance without measure — costs beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，詔毀之，免其官。

translations.literal: Taizong was enraged, ordered it demolished, and removed Jin from office.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's wrath brought an order to tear it all down and dismiss Jin from office.

sentences.zh: 以酆王納璡女為妃，復位。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Feng took Jin's daughter as consort, Jin was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Feng took Jin's daughter as consort, Jin was restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of rites, posthumously titled An.

sentences.zh: 璡有巧思，工書。

translations.literal: Jin had ingenious ideas and was skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Jin possessed ingenious talent and excelled at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 武德中，與太常少卿祖孝孫受詔定雅樂，是正鐘律雲。

translations.literal: In Wude, together with Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zu Xiaosun he received an edict to fix court music and correct the pitch pipes and tonal scales.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude he and Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zu Xiaosun were ordered to establish court music and correct the pitch pipes and tonal standards.

sentences.zh: 從孫 德玄

translations.literal: Grandnephew: Dexuan
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew — Dexuan

sentences.zh: 威從孫德玄，隋大業中，起家國學生。

translations.literal: Wei's grandnephew Dexuan, in the Daye era under Sui, entered office as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan, grandnephew of Wei, entered service during Sui Daye as a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 祖照，尚周文帝義陽公主，封钜鹿郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was enfeoffed Duke of Julu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang of Northern Zhou and was enfeoffed duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 父彥，襲爵，終隋西平太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan inherited the title and ended as Administrator of Xiping under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan inherited the title and ended his career as Sui administrator of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 兄德明，師事陳留王孝逸，通知文史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and was well versed in literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and was accomplished in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，遣將綦良攻黎州。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he dispatched the general Qi Liang to attack Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent General Qi Liang against Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 德明年十八，募士五千，號令嚴整，倍道擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Deming was eighteen; he recruited five thousand men, his orders strict and orderly; marching day and night he struck the rebels and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Deming, only eighteen, raised five thousand men, drilled them to strict discipline, and marching at forced pace routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以功擢累齊王府屬。

translations.literal: For his merit he was repeatedly promoted as staff member of the Prince of Qi's household.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory he rose through posts on the staff of the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵叩長安，而宗室孝基、神符、道宗及竇誕、趙慈景等並系獄，隋將衛文升、陰世師欲殺之，德明諫曰：「罪不在此，殺之無傷於彼，祗取怨焉，不如縱之。」
