translations.literal: When Gaozu's army reached Chang'an, the imperial clansmen Xiaoji, Shenfu, Daozong, Dou Dan, Zhao Cijing, and others were all imprisoned; the Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wished to kill them; Deming remonstrated: "The crime does not lie with these men — killing them will not harm the enemy, and will only win hatred; better to release them."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's army reached Chang'an, the imperial clansmen Xiaoji, Shenfu, Daozong, Dou Dan, Zhao Cijing, and others languished in prison. The Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wanted them executed. Deming urged: "The guilt does not lie with these men — killing them will not weaken the enemy, only breed hatred. Better to set them free."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They desisted.

sentences.zh: 長安平，謁高祖，終不自言，時稱長者。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, he called on Gaozu but never spoke of himself; the age called him a man of rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an fell, he paid his respects to Gaozu yet never once mentioned his own deeds — men of the time hailed him as a man of true dignity.

sentences.zh: 拜考功郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made gentleman of the bureau of merit.

sentences.zh: 從秦王擊王世充。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin he attacked Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with the Prince of Qin against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 封顯武男，曆常、愛二州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Baron of Xianwu and successively served as Prefect of Chang and Ai; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed baron of Xianwu, served as prefect of Chang and Ai in turn, and died.

sentences.zh: 德玄始為高祖丞相府千牛，曆太宗時不甚顯，高宗以舊臣，自殿中少監為御史大夫，歲中遷司元太常伯。

translations.literal: Dexuan first served as Thousand-Bull officer in Gaozu's chancellor's office; through Taizong's reign he was not greatly prominent; Gaozong, honoring him as an old minister, promoted him from Vice Director of the Palace Department to Censor-in-Chief, and within the year transferred him to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan began as a thousand-bull officer in Gaozu's chancellor's office and remained relatively obscure through Taizong's reign. Honoring him as an old minister, Gaozong raised him from vice director of the palace department to censor-in-chief and within a year moved him to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時帝又以源直心為奉常正卿，劉祥道為司刑太常伯，上官儀為西台侍極，郝處俊為太子左中護，凡十餘人，皆帝自擇，以示宰相李勣等，皆頓首謝。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor also appointed Yuan Zhixin Director of Ceremonies, Liu Xiangdao Vice Minister of Justice, Shangguan Yi Attendant of the Western Secretariat, and Hao Chujun Left Protector of the Heir Apparent — more than ten persons in all, all personally chosen by the Emperor, shown to the Chancellor Li Ji and others, who all kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also personally selected more than ten men — Yuan Zhixin as director of ceremonies, Liu Xiangdao as vice minister of justice, Shangguan Yi as attendant of the western secretariat, Hao Chujun as left protector of the heir apparent — and presented them to Chancellor Li Ji and his colleagues, who all bowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，進檢校左相，勤職約己，天子嘗臨朝，咨其清素，加以賜賚。

translations.literal: At the start of Linde he was advanced to Acting Left Chancellor; diligent in office and sparing toward himself — the Son of Heaven once attended court and inquired about his integrity and frugality, and added grants and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Linde he was made acting left chancellor. Diligent in duty and austere in his habits, he was once questioned at audience about his integrity and plain living, and the emperor rewarded him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 居位數年，贊圖封禪事，與李勣皆為使。

translations.literal: After several years in office he assisted in planning the feng and shan rites; he and Li Ji both served as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he helped plan the feng and shan sacrifices; he and Li Ji both served as ritual envoys.

sentences.zh: 帝次濮陽，問古謂帝丘，德玄不能對，許敬宗具道其然，帝稱善。

translations.literal: When the Emperor stopped at Puyang, he asked whether in antiquity it was called Diqiu; Dexuan could not answer; Xu Jingzong fully explained that this was so, and the Emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Stopping at Puyang, the emperor asked whether the place had anciently been called Diqiu. Dexuan could not answer, but Xu Jingzong explained the matter in full, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 敬宗自矜於人，德玄知，不為忤，眾服其量。

translations.literal: Jingzong was self-congratulatory before others; Dexuan knew this yet did not take offense; the multitude admired his forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong habitually flaunted his knowledge before others. Dexuan understood this yet never took umbrage, and all admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進爵二級。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, his noble rank was advanced two steps.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, his noble rank rose two steps.

sentences.zh: 以弟德遠未及爵，願分封，詔可，故德玄封钜鹿男，德遠樂安男。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Deyuan had not yet received a noble title, he requested a division of enfeoffment; the edict approved, so Dexuan was enfeoffed Baron of Julu and Deyuan Baron of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger brother Deyuan had not yet received a title, Dexuan asked to split his enfeoffment. The emperor assented: Dexuan became baron of Julu, Deyuan baron of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 德玄迎時取合，未嘗有過，然無它補益。

translations.literal: Dexuan accommodated himself to the times and never transgressed, yet made no other contribution.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan kept in step with the times and never gave offense, yet offered no further service of note.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九，贈光祿大夫，幽州都督，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine and was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Military Governor of You Prefecture, with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine and was posthumously made grand master of splendid happiness and military governor of You, posthumously titled Gong.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高、竇雖緣外戚姻家，然自以才猷結天子，廁跡名臣，垂榮無窮，時有遇合，故見諸事業。

translations.literal: Commentary: Though the Gao and Dou clans owed their standing to ties of affinal kinship, they won the Son of Heaven through their own talent and planning, took place among celebrated ministers, and gained endless glory — each seized the moment when fortune met merit, and so their achievements were recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Though the Gao and Dou families rose through marriage alliances with the throne, they won imperial favor by their own talent and design, took their places among the great ministers, and won lasting honor. Each found the moment when aptitude met opportunity — and so their deeds live in the record.

sentences.zh: 古來賢豪，不遭與運，埋光鏟采，與草木俱腐者，可勝吒哉！

translations.literal: Since antiquity, how many worthy and heroic men, failing to meet their time, have buried their light and hidden their luster, rotting with the grass and trees — who can exhaust all exclamation and lament!
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, how many worthy and heroic men never met their season, buried their brilliance and hid their luster, and rotted away with the grass and trees — the count is beyond exclamation and lament!

sentences.zh: 竇宗自魏訖唐，支胄扶疏數百年，所馮厚矣。

translations.literal: The Dou lineage from Wei through Tang — its branches flourished for several centuries; the footing on which it rested was deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Tang the Dou clan spread its branches for centuries — the foundation it rested upon ran deep indeed.
